#### Section 1

```{r}
traffic <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\gardu\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\MATH449\\Data\\Traffic_Crashes_-_Crashes.csv")
nrow(traffic)
traffic <- na.omit(traffic)
nrow(traffic)
# 1 if there's any injury, 0 otherwise
traffic$INJURY_ANY <- as.factor(ifelse(traffic$INJURIES_TOTAL > 0, 1, 0))

# key predictors
df_clean <- traffic %>%
  select(
    INJURY_ANY,
    POSTED_SPEED_LIMIT,
    WEATHER_CONDITION,
    LIGHTING_CONDITION,
    ROADWAY_SURFACE_COND,
    CRASH_HOUR,
    CRASH_DAY_OF_WEEK,
    LANE_CNT  
  )

df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

# sample to capture try and capture all factor levels
set.seed(17)
sample_idx <- createDataPartition(df_clean$INJURY_ANY, p = 50000 / nrow(df_clean), list = FALSE)
df_sample <- df_clean[sample_idx, ]

# Plots
ggplot(df_clean, aes(x = POSTED_SPEED_LIMIT, fill = INJURY_ANY)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, position = "stack", color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("0" = "salmon", "1" = "turquoise3"), 
                    labels = c("Property Damage Only", "Injury Occurred")) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Posted Speed Limits by Crash Outcome",
       x = "Posted Speed Limit (MPH)", y = "Count of Crashes", fill = "Outcome") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(df_clean, aes(x = LIGHTING_CONDITION, fill = INJURY_ANY)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("0" = "salmon", "1" = "turquoise3"), 
                    labels = c("Property Damage Only", "Injury Occurred")) +
  labs(title = "Proportional Injury Rates Across Lighting Conditions",
       x = "Lighting Condition", y = "Proportion of Crashes", fill = "Outcome") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Reshape data slightly just for quick plotting of frequencies
df_clean %>%
  select(WEATHER_CONDITION, ROADWAY_SURFACE_COND) %>%
  gather(key = "Environmental_Predictor", value = "Condition Value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = `Condition Value`)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "salmon", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~Environmental_Predictor, scales = "free_x", nrow = 2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Frequencies of Atmospheric and Road Surface Conditions",
       x = "Condition Category", y = "Crash Counts")
```

Vehicle collisions are a very common occurring issue, especially in large and busy cities such as Chicago. While every traffic accident is different, the severity of the collisions varies. Some collisions result in minor property damage only while others result in severe bodily injuries or even fatalities. In order to have safer streets and improve emergency response deployment, it is important to identify the specific environmental, weather, and structural factors that contribute to injury severity during a collision. In this project, the factors influencing whether a collision results in physical injury will be analyzed through logistic regression, utilizing binary injury occurrence as the target variable.

#### Section 2

```{r}
full_model <- glm(INJURY_ANY ~ POSTED_SPEED_LIMIT + WEATHER_CONDITION + 
                  LIGHTING_CONDITION + ROADWAY_SURFACE_COND + 
                  CRASH_HOUR + CRASH_DAY_OF_WEEK + LANE_CNT, 
                  data = df_sample, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
summary(full_model)
```

#### Section 3

```{r}
best_model <- step(full_model, direction = "both", trace = FALSE)
summary(best_model)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(best_model) 
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Goodness of Fit
gof_p_value <- 1 - pchisq(best_model$deviance, best_model$df.residual)
gof_p_value

# Odds Ratios and CI's
odds_ratios <- exp(coef(best_model))
ci_mult_effects <- exp(confint(best_model))

print(cbind(Odds_Ratio = odds_ratios, ci_mult_effects))

```

#### Section 4

```{r}
set.seed(994)
test_data <- df_clean[-sample_idx, ] %>% sample_n(1000)

# predicted probabilities
test_data$pred_prob <- predict(best_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")

# first few predictions
head(test_data[, c("INJURY_ANY", "pred_prob")])

```

#### Section 5

```{r}
cutoffs <- c(0.10, 0.20, 0.50)

for(pi_0 in cutoffs) {
  pi_0
  
  pred_class <- as.factor(ifelse(test_data$pred_prob > pi_0, 1, 0))
  levels(pred_class) <- c("0", "1") 
  
  cm <- confusionMatrix(pred_class, test_data$INJURY_ANY, positive = "1")
  print(cm$table)
  cat("Accuracy:", cm$overall["Accuracy"], " | Sensitivity:", cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], " | Specificity:", cm$byClass["Specificity"], "\n")
}

```

#### Section 6

```{r}
# probability of injury across speed limits
ggplot(df_sample, aes(x = POSTED_SPEED_LIMIT, y = as.numeric(INJURY_ANY)-1)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.05, alpha = 0.2, color = "darkgray") +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"), color = "blue", se = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Logistic Regression Curve: Probability of Injury vs Speed Limit",
       x = "Posted Speed Limit (MPH)", y = "Probability of Injury (1 = Yes)") +
  theme_minimal()

# proportion of injuries across weather conditions
ggplot(df_sample, aes(x = WEATHER_CONDITION, fill = INJURY_ANY)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Proportion of Crash Severity by Weather Condition",
       x = "Weather Condition", y = "Proportion", fill = "Injury Occurred") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```

#### Section 7

```{r}
roc_obj <- roc(test_data$INJURY_ANY, test_data$pred_prob)

# ROC Curve
plot(roc_obj, col = "salmon", main = paste("ROC Curve (AUC =", round(auc(roc_obj), 4), ")"), lwd = 2)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 2, col = "gray")

# best cutoff point
best_coords <- coords(roc_obj, "best", ret = c("threshold", "specificity", "sensitivity"))
print(best_coords)
```

#### Section 8

```{r}
cost_fn <- function(r, pi = 0) mean(abs(r - pi) > 0.5)

# k-Fold Cross-Validation (k = 10)
set.seed(123)
cv_10fold <- cv.glm(df_sample, best_model, cost = cost_fn, K = 10)
cat("10-Fold CV Misclassification Error Rate:", cv_10fold$delta[1], "\n")

# LOOCV
df_loocv <- df_sample %>% sample_n(500)
loocv_model <- glm(formula(best_model), data = df_loocv, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
cv_loocv <- cv.glm(df_loocv, loocv_model, cost = cost_fn)
cat("LOOCV Misclassification Error Rate:", cv_loocv$delta[1], "\n")

```

#### Section 9

```{r}
# Probit Link Model
probit_model <- glm(formula(best_model), data = df_sample, family = binomial(link = "probit"))
summary(probit_model)

# Identity Link Model
model_coefficients_count <- length(coef(best_model))
start_vals <- c(mean(as.numeric(df_sample$INJURY_ANY) - 1), rep(0, model_coefficients_count - 1))

identity_model <- glm(formula(best_model), data = df_sample, 
                      family = binomial(link = "identity"), 
                      start = start_vals, 
                      control = glm.control(maxit = 100))
summary(identity_model)

# compare using AIC
cat("Logit Link AIC   :", AIC(best_model), "\n")
cat("Probit Link AIC  :", AIC(probit_model), "\n")
cat("Identity Link AIC:", AIC(identity_model), "\n")

```

#### Section 10

The Probit link model achieved the lowest overall AIC score at 37060.02. However, because the difference between the Probit and Logit models is only 0.14 points, they're almost identical in predictive performance. We also have to take into consideration that Logit coefficients can give us Odds Ratios which help us with interpretations in our context.
